Entities / Vehicles / The Bad Receipt

The Bad Receipt

Read Aloud

A two-masted schooner cuts low through the channel under patched cream canvas and a merchant pennant that looks correct until it matters. Her hull is black-green, stained like old ink, with removable brass registry plates bolted over older scars. When the side screens drop, cannon mouths show in a neat row beneath cargo netting, and the figurehead resolves into a carved clerk holding a ship’s hook behind his back.

Overview

The Bad Receipt is a Tier 2 armed pirate schooner built for Midchain work: false papers, quick pursuit, selective violence, and retreat through channels where Crown captains start arguing with their own charts. She was refitted at Kalowe from a seized courier hull.

She is not a slaughter ship. Her captain wants cargo, letters of marque, ransomable officers, and anything whose owner cannot report the theft without explaining why it was aboard. The crew prefers a disabled rudder, a terrified deck, and a signed transfer under duress.

Operational Notes

Preferred hunting ground: Midchain approaches to the Central Strait, eastbound traffic that has already paid Tidefall fees.

Opening move: Raise false colours, ask for assistance, present a paperwork problem, fire into rigging once the target slows.

Escape plan: Fog Cannon, Ghost Keel, and reef pilots.

Legal posture: Maintains three competing paper identities — distressed courier, Chain Council survey vessel, and privateer under a commission whose issuing island denies knowing it.

DM Note

As an enemy: Tier 2 pirate escalation after the party has outgrown cutter-scale threats. As a prize: complete mid-campaign ship bastion — useful, compromised, and immediately wanted by somebody. As a contact: buys silence, sells papers, and knows which captains carry cargo they cannot report stolen.

Active Situations

  • Kalowe — The Bad Receipt’s Cache — Nine crates of prize cargo stashed on a nameless limestone rock 3 miles east of Kalowe. The pilot who knew the location is dead; Orina Fale has been trying to recover it for eight months. A fisherman named Damu knows where the rock is.
